claim: Philosophical theories of content fall into four families (informational, teleological/consumer, conceptual-role, resemblance/structural); no theory is accepted, and each faces a named problem (disjunction, Swampman, holism, indeterminacy).
agent_test: Use the map as a checklist: for each restated problem in S2, ask what the restatement is caused by, used by, and structurally mirrors. Compare S2 with and without a 'what will later steps do with this' line at equal tokens.

claim: Information alone is not enough for content: a state can carry information (smoke, tree trunks, thermostat) without representing; a representation must also be used by a consumer for a function.
agent_test: Score whether downstream steps change when the S2 restatement is edited (consumer-use), versus restatements that merely paraphrase.

claim: Decodability is not use: a probe reading a variable shows information is present, not that the model uses it. Probe-based claims need controls (random-network baseline, control tasks, selectivity) and interventions.
agent_test: Do not trust a self-reported 'I represented X'; edit X in the scratch state and see whether the answer changes.

claim: Probe expressiveness changes the answer: an MLP probe on POS tagging reaches 97.3% task vs 92.8% control (selectivity 4.5), while a linear probe reaches 97.2% vs 71.2% (selectivity 26.0). High accuracy alone is misleading.
agent_test: Not directly testable on the agent; informs how we score any probe-like analysis of agent traces.

claim: A GPT trained only on Othello move text builds an internal board state: top-1 illegal-move rate 0.01% (20M synthetic games), 5.17% (championship), 93.29% untrained; nonlinear probe error falls to 1.7%; activation edits change predicted moves (0.12 vs 2.68 errors null).
agent_test: Analogue: does the agent keep an explicit state (board, constraints) across steps, and does editing it change later moves? Small grid puzzle set, state-in-scratchpad vs none, equal tokens.

claim: Li et al.'s 'linear probes fail' result was a coding artefact: coded relative to the player (MINE/YOURS/EMPTY) the board is linear (99.5-99.6% peak vs about 75% for BLACK/WHITE); linear interventions work as well as nonlinear (0.10 vs 0.12 errors, null 2.72).
agent_test: Lesson: the representation that fits the consumer's perspective (mover-relative) is easier. Test: restate in the actor's frame vs an absolute frame.

claim: The board-state result generalises to chess trained on real human games: legal-move rate 99.8% (16-layer), board probe 99.6% (random net 74.7%), win rate 64% vs Stockfish level 0; a latent skill variable is also encoded (probe 90.5% vs 69.3% random); editing gives legal moves 92.0% vs 40.5% without.
agent_test: Latent variables beyond the surface state may be tracked; test an S2 slot for hidden variables (asker intent, hidden constraints) for added accuracy.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Real-world structure is linearly decodable from LLM activations: Llama-2-70b linear probe out-of-sample R2 0.911 (world places), 0.864 (USA), 0.359 (NYC), 0.835 (historical figures dates); MLP adds little; larger models are better.
agent_test: Do not expect fine-grained (NYC level) accuracy even at 70B. Behavioural test: ask for coordinates at city vs district grain.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Truth has a roughly linear direction in LLaMA-2 that sharpens with scale, and mass-mean probes are more causally effective than logistic regression despite similar accuracy.
agent_test: Do not build a verifier on this claim; test whether the agent's self-verification beats a no-verify arm at equal tokens.

claim: Unsupervised truth probes (CCS) do not find knowledge: with distractor insertion ground-truth accuracy falls to 50% for CCS, PCA, K-means; CCS on LLaMA-30B is 50-57% (chance 50%); supervised probes fail on negations (5 of 6 worse than chance).
agent_test: Warns against internal consistency as a truth signal. Test self-consistency voting vs an external check on items with an injected salient distractor.

claim: Marks and Tegmark respond that negation failure shrinks with scale and with training on statements plus their negations, so truth-direction failure is partly a data-diversity effect.
agent_test: Levinstein's rebuttal not read in full; test only if we build truth probes.

claim: Accuracy and probes can coexist with an incoherent world model: NYC taxi transformers have next-token validity 1.00 and state-probe 0.91-0.99 but compression precision 0.05-0.50 and distinction recall 0.35-0.99; the shortest-path model's valid traversals fall to 0.08 at moderate detour rates.
agent_test: Test the agent's state with detour/perturbation items: same state reached by different routes must give same continuations. Report failure rate at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Prompted LLMs also show weak world-model coherence: GPT-4 seating puzzle compression 0.21, distinction 0.56; GPT-3.5 compression 0.33, distinction 0.18. GPT-4 simulates 77.1% of action-driven but at most 49.7% of environment-driven text-game transitions.
agent_test: Use as baselines for our own state-tracking test; expect environment-driven changes to be lost unless S2 lists them explicitly.

claim: Models define concepts correctly (94.2%) yet fail to use them (potemkin rate 0.55 classification, 0.40 generation, 0.40 editing; lower bound 0.62 on MMLU-derived self-consistency). Stating a representation in words is not the same as using it.
agent_test: Add a use-check: after S2 states a concept or rule, apply it to a fresh instance; measure the potemkin gap with and without the check.

claim: Representations in different models converge with scale (language-vision mutual nearest-neighbour alignment rises with capability), and text-only LMs align with CIELAB colour space. Effects are small (alignment about 0.1-0.3; colour RSA tau 0.16-0.33; fastText baseline already 0.23).
agent_test: Not decision-relevant for the scaffold.

claim: Philosophical positions on LLM meaning are split and not settled by these data: Bender and Koller (form alone cannot yield meaning), Piantadosi and Hill (conceptual role), Mollo and Milliere (grounding needs selection history), Mandelkern and Linzen (externalist reference); a survey of 480 NLP researchers split 51% vs 49%.
agent_test: Not testable; it frames which criteria we adopt (information, consumer use, misrepresentation).

claim: Philosophers' criteria for an activation pattern to represent a feature are (a) carries information, (b) influences behaviour in a task-relevant way, (c) the system can misrepresent. Most LLM studies test (a), some (b), almost none (c).
agent_test: Test (c): can the agent flag a restatement as wrong (misrepresentation detection) at equal tokens.

claim: Explicit world-model prompting helps planning for small models: RAP (LLM as world model plus MCTS) reaches Blocksworld 2/4/6-step success 1.00/0.86/0.26 (RAP(10)) vs CoT LLaMA-33B 0.17/0.02/0.00; but GPT-4 CoT scores 0.50/0.63/0.40, above RAP(10) at 6 steps.
agent_test: Run explicit-state-prediction arm vs plain CoT at equal tokens; gain is model-dependent.

claim: Theory predicts, and one study shows, that sequence models keep belief-state geometry over hidden states: fit R2 0.95 vs 0.31 for next-token geometry on RRXOR. New: prompted LLMs given a hidden user preference over 5 rounds plateau after round 1 (about 36-58% vs Bayesian 81%), and CoT did not help (d09); per-character belief structure is causally traced in open models up to 405B (d12, d13).
agent_test: Idea only: states should encode uncertainty over hidden causes. Test a small weighted hypothesis set vs a single guess in S2.

claim: Belief depth varies by method: prompting a fact generalises to related tasks but collapses under adversarial scrutiny and debate, while synthetic-document fine-tuning persists on most facts (Llama 3.3 70B), so a stated representation can be shallow.
agent_test: Prompt-stated S2 content should be pressure-tested (ask for the source line, then contradict it) before later steps rely on it. Numbers in d15 are mostly in figures.

claim: Self-conditioning: in long multi-step runs, models are more likely to err when their context holds their own earlier errors; a restatement copied forward from an earlier erroneous step propagates the error. Thinking mode and shrinking the context window mitigate it; a self-verify prompt does not fully.
agent_test: Compare re-deriving S2 from the source problem each step vs copying forward the previous S2, on a long task at equal tokens. Track error carry-over.
limits: Sinha (synthetic task, open models plus frontier horizon table) and Shojaee (puzzles) agree that long-run failures occur, but disagree on cause; both are puzzle or synthetic tasks.

claim: Same-model review of its own output is a weak error detector: intrinsic self-correction lowered accuracy (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 after two rounds), and GPT-4 finds the first mistake in a CoT trace only 39.8-52.9% of the time; given the error location, correction works.
agent_test: Test 'is this restatement wrong?' vs 'does slot k match source line j?' on seeded misstatements. Measure detection rate and false alarms.
limits: 2023 models; later models and RL training may do better (not tested here).

claim: Stated reasoning can misrepresent what drove the answer: biasing features in the prompt change answers (accuracy down by up to 36% on 13 BBH tasks) and the chain of thought rationalises them without mention.
agent_test: Edit one input feature (answer order, a hint) and check whether the S2 restatement changes. If not, do not treat S2 as the cause.
limits: GPT-3.5 and Claude 1.0 only; 'up to' is the worst case.

claim: Behavioural distractor failure is real and partly fixed by agreement: irrelevant sentences cut GSM-IC macro accuracy to 6.0% (COT, code-davinci-002); self-consistency over 20 samples lifts LTM micro accuracy to 93.4% and macro accuracy to 45%; an ignore-irrelevant instruction gives +5 to +8 points. This differs from probes (Farquhar), where unsupervised agreement fails.
agent_test: Add a distractor sentence to inputs; compare accuracy with S2 that keeps only relevant quantities vs full free restatement.

claim: Structured compact state can beat free-text steps where text is ambiguous: Chain-of-Symbol raised GPT-3.5 Brick World accuracy 31.8% to 92.6% with up to 65.8% fewer input tokens, but gains on natural SPARTUN were small (GPT-4 69.8 to 72.6). Tracking entity state in context needs code-trained GPT-3.5-class models. No study compares typed slots with free restatement for frontier models at equal tokens.
agent_test: Ablation: typed slots vs free restatement vs none, equal tokens, on state-tracking and relational tasks; run with two frontier models.
limits: Evidence is on GPT-3.5/GPT-4-era models; the central gap-1 question remains untested for frontier prompted models.

claim: Pretrained models do not maintain weighted hypotheses by default: they keep roughly a single best guess and plateau after round 1; teaching them to mimic a Bayesian assistant (fine-tuning, not prompting) lifts agreement with Bayes to about 80%.
agent_test: Store a small weighted hypothesis list in S2 and update it by explicit rule after each observation; compare with a single-guess S2 on a hidden-preference task.
limits: Fine-tuning result; prompting-only scaffolds untested here. Single synthetic domain with transfer.

claim: Teleosemantic reading of LLMs rests on selection history; training (including RLHF) counts as selection on Garson-style and learning-based accounts, but no experiment tests this directly. The closest contrast (Slocum) fits it: prompted facts are shallower than trained ones. Primary texts by Fodor, Dretske, Millikan and Block still known only via SEP.
agent_test: Do not build agent design on selection-history claims; use only the testable parts (use by a consumer, robustness under pushback).
limits: Philosophical; Mollo and Millière give no numbers; SEP is secondary.

claim: Interpretability replications in 2025 mostly extend rather than contradict the Othello findings: seven LMs trained on Othello align at up to 99% in unsupervised grounding (Yuan and Sogaard), and causal belief-tracking mechanisms are traced in Llama-3.1-405B (Prakash). Nothing found tests Othello/chess-style world models in closed frontier models, and the Vafa coherence failures are not refuted.
agent_test: Not an agent test; use as a caution that open-model results may not transfer to frontier prompted models.
limits: Open-weight models; alignment is not a causal test.
